b: The Salesforce FIDE World Championship is not only a match between two elite players. It is also an opportunity to explore chess through data.

The official website's Chess by the Numbers section turns more than a decade of FIDE tournament, rating and player data into an interactive experience, oﬀering a unique look at how the game has evolved over the years.

Chess by the Numbers is made possible through FIDE's partnership with Salesforce. Salesforce technology powers real-time rankings, historical player data, predictive analysis and new ways for fans to engage with the game.
Agentforce, the #1 agentic platform powering the digital workforce, helps transform vast amounts of chess data into accessible, interactive insights for fans around the world.

Underpinning this, Data 360 unifies fragmented data from FIDE's player database and 60,000+ annual event streams into real-time fan and player profiles, giving Agentforce the trusted foundation it needs to deliver insights at scale.

Curious how your rating compares to other players? Want to see how strong national federations are, how the player population has grown or which countries host the most rated events? The statistical pages provide dozens of ways to explore the numbers behind the game.

Visitors can browse interactive charts tracking long-term trends and discover how the global chess community has changed over time. The pages also reveal fascinating demographic insights, from the number of rated players in different countries to the growth of chess participation over the last decade.

For example, can you answer this question: what percentage of all rated players were women in 2015? Less than 7%, between 7% and 15%, between 15% and 25%, or more than 25%? And what about today, in 2026? Has the share increased or decreased, and by how much? The answer can be found in the Women tab, and it may surprise you.

For fans of elite chess, dedicated ranking charts showcase the leading players in standard, rapid and blitz. The upcoming World Championship match is also in the spotlight, with the site featuring the head-to-head record between Gukesh and Sindarov.

What would your guess be? How many games have Gukesh and Sindarov played against each other across all time controls? Fewer than five, between five and ten, or more than ten? Who leads the rivalry, and by how many points? The answers can be found in the Head-to-Head tab, where you can also compare other players and explore their records against one another.

The World Championship tab offers a journey through championship history, featuring every World Championship match. Do you know which title match was the longest in history? The answer is the 1984 World Championship match between Kasparov and Karpov, which lasted 48 games and was never completed.
What makes these pages particularly engaging is that they invite exploration. There is always another statistic to uncover and another trend to investigate.
